summary: The first episode of the series, and the comment section shows the audience arriving already sorted by member: separate threads declare themselves Dream fans or Goy fans within the first day. The most-liked comments are from celebrity friends — Violette Wautier and Nicky Nachat — which put the channel's network at the top of the thread from episode one. The most useful cluster is unpaid production consulting: viewers report that the sound effects are mixed louder than the dialogue, and two separate comments tell them to wear seatbelts while filming in the car, one explicitly arguing that road-safety compliance is what will let car sponsors come in. A nostalgia cluster is about the guest, Kao, whom viewers have followed since he was a child actor. Guest requests for future episodes start here and never stop.

audience_signals: The audience gives free, actionable production feedback — audio mix and on-camera road safety — and one commenter explicitly ties compliance to winning car sponsors, so they think commercially about the channel
Member-level fandoms existed from episode one rather than forming over time, which supports member-led formats from the start
Celebrity friends' comments occupy the top slots by likes; that network is a structural amplifier the channel gets for free
The guest-request habit begins in episode one and is still running at episode 102 — a continuous demand signal worth mining
A five-year-old first episode still holds 5.6M views, so the back catalogue keeps working as an entry point for new viewers
content_requests: Raise dialogue level relative to sound effects
Wear seatbelts while filming in the car
Book Mario and Fey as guests
Keep the episode length as it is
